story.titleZh: “不是朝九晚五的巡航”——从零组建凯迪拉克赛道团队的回报性挑战
story.summaryZh: 凯迪拉克在加入2026年F1赛程前一年开始寻找车队经理，很快锁定了哈斯车队长期任职的车队经理彼得·克罗拉。克罗拉寻求新挑战，并期待再次从零组建团队的机会。
story.originalTitle: "No nine to five cruise" - The rewarding challenge of assembling Cadillac's trackside team from scratch
story.summaryEn: Cadillac began searching for a race team manager a full year before joining the 2026 Formula 1 grid and quickly identified long-serving Haas team manager Peter Crolla. Crolla was looking for a new challenge and saw the chance to build another team from the ground up as the perfect fit.
detailZh: “不是朝九晚五的悠闲差事”——从零组建凯迪拉克赛道车队的艰巨而值得的挑战
车队经理彼得·克罗拉敞开心扉，谈凯迪拉克成为一支受人尊敬的F1车队所经历的艰难历程
当全新加入的凯迪拉克开始寻找一位车队经理时——距离它加入2026年F1发车区还有整整一年——它不必花很长时间、也不必看很远，就锁定了合适的人选。
而在哈斯——F1上一支2016年才起步的车队——长期任职的车队经理彼得·克罗拉正在寻找新的挑战，再次从零开始打造一支车队的机会正合他的心意。
在与格雷姆·洛登进行早期沟通后，克罗拉开始了又一次全新的起点，在九个月的时间里从零开始组建一支赛道边团队。洛登最近被马尔钦·布德科夫斯基取代车队领队一职，但他一直是凯迪拉克在一级方程式中取得体面首秀背后的关键推动力。
"在那个时候，我已经在哈斯车队工作了九年多，我确实准备好迎接改变和新的挑战，我需要一些东西来重新点燃我对这项运动的热情，"克罗拉在最近的一级方程式比利时大奖赛期间、就在车队领导层变动之前告诉Motorsport.com。
"我喜欢组建车队这件事。这会带来巨大的自豪感，而且所有事情都在合适的时机恰好转到了一起。这是我第二次参与新车队的创建，大概间隔了十年，这真的非常棒。做这件事所带来的冲劲、自主权和兴奋感是无与伦比的。
"那九个月大概是我职业生涯中最愉快的时光，从面对一栋空楼和一个计划开始，并被赋予那样的权力去实现你自己的愿景。"
凯迪拉克车队的比赛团队经理彼得·克罗拉（右）与前任领队格雷姆·洛登、技术顾问帕特·西蒙兹以及瓦尔特利·博塔斯
比赛团队经理是一项职责范围极其广泛且多样的工作，首先要负责车队的整体组织事务。当赛事前的后勤工作处理完毕后，一旦赛道上的行动开始，这份工作就会转向更多与竞技相关的角色，其中包括与管理机构国际汽联（FIA）以及F1管理层进行联络。
但从零开始组建一支新车队，为这份工作增添了庞大的基础性层面。克罗拉借鉴了他在哈斯车队的经验，在凯迪拉克再次尝试这样的壮举——考虑到F1新加入者的稀缺性，这是一次非常难得的机会。
“那时候这项运动的面貌非常不同，”克罗拉回顾当年帮助哈斯车队从无到有时说道，“我们还处在伯尼·埃克莱斯顿的时代。规模是一件很重要的事，而且那也是我第一次做这种事，非常令人兴奋。在那段时间里，我和一些很出色的人共事，学到了很多。我认为这为我第二次做这件事打下了良好的基础。”
当被问及在哈斯车队学到的关键经验是什么时，克罗拉回答说：“我认为在那段时间里，赛历和车队所面临的要求都不断增长，我想确保我们以一支大车队的姿态来应对这件事，并且拥有出色完成这项任务所需的一切。
“在我看来，这从来都不是先从小规模做起再逐步壮大的问题。因为没有时间这样做，因为一旦你开始参赛，你能花在各个项目上的时间就会大大减少。所以对我来说，关键在于尽我们所能把每一件事做到最好，充分利用我们可用的预算，打造一支随时可以参赛并把它做好的车队。
“对我来说，这第一年需要有三大支柱。第一是体面地参与比赛。也就是说，我们准时出现在赛场，把所有该做的事情做对，保持低调。我认为我们做到了这一点。第二个支柱是可靠性，可以肯定的是，我们仍在为此努力。第三个是性能，我们也已经进入了这个阶段。所以，一切都在按我的预期进行。到目前为止，一切顺利，我想这么说。
当克罗拉在四月加入时，位于银石的工厂基地已经就绪，但那支将环游世界的赛道团队还只是一张白纸。随后，克罗拉与其他新加入的成员——车队物流经理皮特·西蒙斯和首席机械师内森·迪维——坐下来，共同规划通往墨尔本的道路。这涵盖了从采购车队所需的硬件设备，到为赛道运作、赛车组装、进站换胎等建立流程和最佳实践——对任何车队来说，这都是一份无尽的挑战清单，更不用说一群从未合作过的人了。
“我们采取了协作的方式，对2026年一支优秀车队应该是什么样子有着共同的愿景，”克罗利亚解释道。“没有现成的教科书，也没有关于如何做到这一点的指导方针，但我们非常努力地工作，而且对于我们想做的事情，几乎没有（如果有的话）任何分歧。
“我们只是知道它必须是最好的，但最重要的是，它必须到位。任何东西不到位都是没有借口的，因为我认为在那九个月里一切都是可以实现的，尤其是考虑到我们所拥有的自主权和预算。我们必须给供应商施加很大压力，但我们合作的是之前合作过的好供应商，是我们信任的人，这一点非常重要。知道你可以依靠谁，以及可以把谁真正逼到极限。”
彼得·克罗利亚此前曾在哈斯车队担任类似职务长达十年。
归根结底，任何一个组织都取决于其人员的素质，一级方程式（F1）也不例外，凯迪拉克组建了一支准备挑战既有势力的车队。考虑到其中涉及的漫长“园艺假”（gardening leave，即离职后的强制等待期），这绝非易事，尤其对于一支还没有任何往绩的车队来说更是如此。
“招聘这件事我们必须非常积极，因为人们都已经处于很长的离职通知期了，”克罗拉指出。“在这个行业里，没有人能在少于三个月内真正到岗，有些人甚至有六个月的离职通知期。”
“很多人是在2025年下半年加入的，根本没有什么蜜月期。他们必须立刻投入进去，把所有事情都干起来。每天都有大量的设备运到门口，工作量极其惊人。但每个人都真正迎接了这一挑战。”
不过，正如这种初创文化吸引了克罗拉加入凯迪拉克的故事一样，许多从F1最大车队跳槽过来的其他新员工似乎也有同感。对于车队将面临的挑战，以及绝不会有一帆风顺这回事，大家心里都很清楚。
“不，我认为如果你从一支成熟车队过来，却以为这里会和原来一样，那就是相当被误导了，”克罗拉点头表示。“我认为人们明白更大的图景：加入这样一个项目，它不会是梅赛德斯，也不会是法拉利，那些家伙已经运营了几十年。但与此同时，只要意识到有机会塑造我们自己的环境，我认为人们就看到了其中的吸引力。”
"从其他组织引进人才的关键，在于认清他们的优势、认清他们的经验，并把这些挖掘出来，打造我们共同的工作流程。从其他车队来到比赛团队和更广泛业务的申请者的质量和数量都非常令人振奋。但这需要一种能够迎接挑战的心态。这不会是一份朝九晚五的轻松工作。而是要深挖潜力，做好长期奋斗的准备。"
"我们所做的一切都没有超出我的预期。我原以为可能会更难一些，也可能以为在某些时候会更令人失望。"——克罗拉。
凯迪拉克在此过程中确实按时完成了每一项内部和外部期限，顺利开始了冬季测试，并在澳大利亚用其中一辆赛车完成了首场比赛。但随后在可靠性和运营方面出现的小毛病，加上在队尾被阿斯顿·马丁超越，进一步表明仅仅参赛只是起点。
"这些里程碑并不容易达成。每一个里程碑背后都真真切切地凝聚着血、汗和泪，"克罗拉回顾道，"它真的会变成你的生活。它必须如此，因为你每天要工作超长时间，还要求其他所有人也同样付出。我认为没有任何其他运动能像这样，当你真正造出一辆赛车并让它第一次驶上赛道时，能亲眼看到自己劳动的成果。那也许只是一个一月里银石赛道阴冷下雨的下午，但那感觉太棒了。它给了所有人一种巨大的成就感。
"毫无疑问，我们遇到了可靠性方面的问题。我认为这对任何人来说都不意外，但关键在于你如何面对它们、如何解决它们、以及如何从中恢复。对我来说，我们所做的一切与我预期的情况并没有脱节。我可能原本预计会更艰难一些，有时也可能预计会更令人失望一些。奥地利站大概算是我们的一个低谷，但这只是旅程的一部分。如果有人对此感到惊讶，那么我认为对我们来说经历这一切可能是一次有益的经验。"
随着凯迪拉克进入下一个阶段，前雷诺人士布德科夫斯基如今执掌车队，车队明年将开始启用位于印第安纳州费舍尔市的全新美国总部，克罗拉坚称那里将是一个"绝佳的运营基地"，同时在未来几个月里还将扩建位于银石赛道的英国基地。
"开始参赛并不是建设和发展这项事业的终点。它其实只是这段旅程中的又一个阶段，我认为要等到所有这些各自独立的部门都全面运转起来，我们才能真正看清我们在这里所做之事的规模，"他补充道。
"这里有一些非常有才华的人才，不过于自夸地说，我们做得不错，但我们才刚刚起步。"
detailEn: "No nine to five cruise" - The rewarding challenge of assembling Cadillac's trackside team from scratch
Race team manager Peter Crolla opens up on Cadillac's challenging journey to becoming a respected Formula 1 team

When brand-new entrant Cadillac started its search for a race team manager, still a full year removed from joining the 2026 Formula 1 grid, it didn't have to look very long, or far, to identify the right target.

Over at Haas, F1's previous start-up team in 2016, long serving team manager Peter Crolla had been looking for a new challenge, and the prospect of another chance to build a team from the ground up was ticking all the right boxes.

Following early conversations with Graeme Lowdon, who was recently replaced by Marcin Budkowski as team principal but has been the instrumental driving force behind Cadillac's respectable F1 debut, Crolla embarked on another fresh start building up a trackside team from scratch over a nine-month period.

"I'd been at Haas for over nine years at that point, and I was definitely ready for a change and a new challenge, and I needed something to get my excitement back for the sport," Crolla old Motorsport.com at the recent Belgian Grand Prix, before the team's leadership change.

"I love the element of setting up a team. There's a great deal of pride in that, and everything just aligned at the right time. It's my second new team start, sort of 10 years apart, and it was absolutely brilliant. The momentum, the autonomy and the excitement of doing that is unparalleled.
"That nine month period was probably the most enjoyable of my career, from starting with an empty building and a plan, and being given that authority to create your vision."
Cadillac race team manager Peter Crolla (right) with former team principal Graeme Lowdon, technical consultant Pat Symonds and Valtteri Bottas

Being a race team manager in a job with an extremely wide and diverse scope, starts with being responsible for the overall organisation of the race team. Once the pre-event logistics are out of the way, the job then shifts into a more sporting oriented role when the on-track action starts, which includes liaising with governing body the FIA and F1 management.

But starting a new team from zero adds a huge foundational layer to that, with Crolla drawing from his experience at Haas to have another go at Cadillac, which is a very rare opportunity in F1 given the scarcity of new entrants.

"The sport was a very different place back then," Crolla said, looking back on helping bring Haas to life. "We were still in the Bernie Ecclestone era. Scale was a big thing, and it was also my first time doing it. It was exciting. I worked with some great people there during that period, and learnt a lot. And I think that set me up well for doing it the second time round."

When asked what his key lessons were from Haas, Crolla replied: "I think the calendar and the requirements on a team have grown over the course of that period, and I wanted to ensure that we approached this as a big team and had everything we needed to accomplish the task well.

"It was, in my opinion, never a case of starting small and then growing. There isn't time for that because once you're out racing, the time you've got to spend on your projects is greatly decreased. So for me, it was about doing everything to the best of our abilities, maximising the budget we had available for it, and just creating a team that was ready to go racing and do a good job of it.

"For me, there were three pillars of how this first year needed to be. It was respectable participation. So, we show up on time, and we do all the right things, keep our heads down. I think we accomplished that. The next pillar was reliability, and for sure we're still working our way through that. And then the third is performance, and we're into that phase as well. So, it's happening as I thought it would. So far so good. I would say."

While the factory-based operation in Silverstone was already in place when Crolla joined in April, the trackside team that would travel the world was still a blank sheet of paper. Crolla subsequently sat down with fellow new hires, team logistics manager Pete Simmons and chief mechanic Nathan Divey, to map out the road to Melbourne. That ranged from acquiring the hardware the team needed to setting up procedures and best practices for trackside operations, car builds, pitstops - an endless list of challenges for any outfit, never mind a team of people that had never worked together before.

"We had a collaborative approach and a collective vision of what a good race team in 2026 needed to look like," Crolla explained. "There's no book. There are no guidelines on how to do this, but we worked very hard and there were very few, if any, disagreements on what we wanted to do.

"We just knew that it had to be the best, but most of all, it had to be there. There were no excuses for anything not being there because I think everything is achievable in those nine months, and especially given the autonomy and the budget we had. We had to put a lot of pressure on suppliers, but we worked with good suppliers that we'd worked with before. People that we trusted, and that was really important. Knowing who you can lean on and who you can really push to the limit."
Peter Crolla previously spent a decade at Haas in a similar role.

Ultimately, any organisation comes down to the quality of its people, and F1 is no different as Cadillac assembled a team ready to take on the establishment. Given the long gardening leave times involved, that was no easy feat, especially for a team that had no track record yet.

"Recruitment was something that we had to be quite aggressive on because people were already on long notice periods," Crolla pointed out. "Nobody's really available in this sport for any less than three months, and some were on six months' notice.

"A lot of people joined in the second half of 2025, and there was no honeymoon period. They had to get stuck in right away and get on with it all. There was a huge amount of equipment coming through the door every day, and a phenomenal workload. But everybody really rose to the challenge."

But just like how the start-up culture attracted Crolla to the Cadillac story, a lot of other hires from F1's biggest teams appeared to feel the same way. There was certainly no mistake on the challenges the team would face, and that there would be no such thing as an easy ride.

"No, I think that would be quite misguided if you came here from an established team and thought it was just going to be like that," Crolla nodded. "I think people understand the bigger picture that coming to a project like this, it's not going to be a Mercedes. It's not going to be a Ferrari where these guys have been in operation for decades. But at the same time, just recognising the opportunity of sculpting our own environment, I think people saw the attraction in that.

"The important part of bringing people in from other organisations is recognising their strengths, recognising their experience, and drawing that out of them to create our combined processes. The quality and quantity of applicants that came into the race team and the wider business from other teams has been really positive. But it needs that mentality that can rise to the challenge. This is not going to be a nine to five cruise. It's digging deep and being in it for the long run."

"Nothing that we've done is out of sync with how I expected it to be. I probably expected it to be a little bit harder, and probably expected it to be a little bit more disappointing at times." - Crolla.

Cadillac did meet every internal and external deadline along the way, making the start of winter testing and finishing its first race in Australia with one of its cars. But subsequent gremlins on the reliability and operational side, while being overtaken by Aston Martin at the rear of the field, have further underlined that simply showing up was just the start.

"Those were not easy milestones to reach. There was literally blood, sweat, and tears for all of them," Crolla reflected. "It turns into your life, really. It has to, because you're working super long days and you're asking everybody else to do the same. I think there's no greater sport where you're able to see the fruits of your labour when you actually build a car that then goes around the track for the first time. It might have been on a rainy cold afternoon in January in Silverstone, but it was mega. It gave everybody a great feeling of achievement.

"For sure, we've come across reliability matters. I don't think that was a surprise to anybody, but it's about how you approach them, how you tackle them, and how you recover from them. For me, nothing that we've done is out of sync with how I expected it to be. I probably expected it to be a little bit harder, and probably expected it to be a little bit more disappointing at times. Austria was probably a bit of a low point for us, but it's just part of the journey. If people were surprised by it, then I think it's probably a useful experience for us to go through."

As Cadillac transitions into its next phase, with former Renault man Budkowski now at the helm, the team will start using a brand-new US headquarters in Fishers, Indiana next year that Crolla insists will be an "amazing place to operate from", while also expanding its UK base in Silverstone in the coming months.

"Starting to go racing is not the end point of building and developing the business. It's really just another stage in that journey, and I think it won't be until all these discrete areas are fully operational that we actually see the scale of what we're doing here," he added.
"There's some really talented people here, and without being overly congratulatory on ourselves, we're doing a good job with it, but we're only just getting started."

relatedItems.summaryEn: Mercedes technical director James Allison has warned that F1 engineers will fight back against the FIA's planned 2027 downforce cuts. detailZh: 梅赛德斯技术总监警告，F1车队不会对2027年下压力削减坐视不管
梅赛德斯技术总监詹姆斯·艾利森警告，F1工程师将对国际汽联2027年的下压力削减予以反击
致梅赛德斯车迷。来自银箭的最新消息，包括F1新闻、车手动态、赛车研发以及来自布拉克利和布里克斯沃思的赛事分析。
F1向2026年新动力单元与底盘规则的过渡彻底打乱了竞争格局，但规则手册远未最终确定。随着车队为2027年新规下的第二个赛季做准备，国际汽联正推动再次强制降低下压力。
早期报告表明，管理机构的目标是在2027赛季将下压力减少20至50个点。为了实现这一目标，国际汽联计划禁止若干关键的后部空气动力学部件，以改善混合动力能量管理，并减少阻碍赛车紧密跟车的湍流“脏空气”。
但梅赛德斯技术总监詹姆斯·艾利森最近警告说，制定规则来减慢一级方程式赛车的速度，很少能阻止围场顶尖工程师找到绕过它的办法。
在NU Silver Arrows Radio Show播客节目中，艾利森确认了国际汽联拟议的空气动力学限制范围，同时向即将到来的研发战发出了挑战。
“我所知道的是，新规则会让赛车损失一些下压力，不止一点，”艾利森解释道。
乔治·拉塞尔，梅赛德斯车队；安德烈亚·基米·安东内利，梅赛德斯车队
从历史上看，国际汽联与一级方程式车队之间的关系始终是一场无休止的猫鼠游戏。管理机构出于安全和竞赛考量修改规则手册以限制过弯速度，而车队则立即在风洞中投入数百万美元，以恢复国际汽联试图削去的下压力。
据艾利森表示，2027年的规则周期也不会有任何不同。
“他们已经做出了不错的尝试，试图将下压力拉回到2026时代初期的水平，”艾利森指出。
他补充道：“看看各车队是会选择妥协接受，还是会全力夺回全部性能，这将非常有意思。”
如果梅赛德斯在2026年的巨大飞跃能说明什么，那就是阿利森在布拉克利的工程部门完全没有妥协的打算。2027赛季的技术战线已经正式划定。
detailEn: Mercedes technical director warns F1 teams won’t “lie down” over 2027 downforce cuts
Mercedes technical director James Allison warns F1 engineers will fight back against the FIA's 2027 downforce cuts
For Mercedes fans. All the latest from the Silver Arrows, with F1 news, driver updates, car development and race analysis from Brackley and Brixworth.

Formula 1's transition to the new 2026 engine and chassis regulations completely reshuffled the competitive order, but the rulebook is far from finalised. As teams prepare for their second year under the new formula in 2027, the FIA is pushing to mandate another drop in downforce.

Early reports indicate the governing body is targeting a reduction of 20 to 50 points of downforce for the 2027 season. To achieve this, the FIA plans to ban several key rear aerodynamic elements in a bid to improve hybrid energy management and reduce the turbulent "dirty air" that prevents cars from following each other closely.
But Mercedes technical director James Allison recently cautioned that writing a rule to slow down a Formula 1 car rarely stops the grid's top engineers from finding a way around it.

Speaking on the NU Silver Arrows Radio Show podcast, Allison confirmed the scope of the FIA's proposed aerodynamic restrictions while simultaneously throwing down the gauntlet for the upcoming development war.
"All I know is that the cars are going to be losing a bit of downforce from the new regs, more than a bit," Allison explained.
George Russell, Mercedes, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes

Historically, the relationship between the FIA and Formula 1 constructors is a perpetual game of cat and mouse. The governing body alters the rulebook to limit cornering speeds on safety and racing grounds, and the teams immediately spend millions of dollars in the wind tunnel to recover the exact downforce the FIA attempted to take away.
According to Allison, the 2027 regulation cycle will be no different.
"They've had a good go at trying to pull the downforce back to [the] start of the 2026 era," Allison noted.
"It'll be interesting to see whether the teams lie down and take that or whether we recover it all or not," he added.

If Mercedes' massive leap forward in 2026 is any indication, Allison's engineering department in Brackley has zero intention of lying down. The technical battle lines for the 2027 season have officially been drawn.

detailZh: 梅赛德斯-奔驰和奥迪在F1拉斯维加斯大奖赛上推出阿迪达斯系列
梅赛德斯-奔驰霓虹灯和奥迪夜场系列现已通过adidas.com购买
拉斯维加斯欢迎标志上空出现彩虹
赛车文化超越赛道。车手生活方式、时尚、旅行、设计和让赛车不仅仅是一项运动的故事。
梅赛德斯-奔驰和奥迪为即将到来的Formula 1拉斯维加斯大奖赛推出了特别的阿迪达斯粉丝系列。
梅赛德斯-奔驰的系列名为"霓虹灯"，而奥迪的系列名为"深夜"。这两个系列现在已在adidas.com上上市，品牌美国店内的单品价格从30美元到200美元不等。
最贵的产品是外套。梅赛德斯-奔驰的拉斯维加斯夹克和奥迪的拉斯维加斯轰炸机夹克都售价200美元。
梅赛德斯-奔驰的系列比奥迪的大。除了夹克，它还包括120美元的卫衣、95美元的长袖T恤、60美元的短裤、55美元的车手帽、50美元的比赛帽和40美元及45美元的T恤。
奥迪车队的阵容有55美元的车手上限，两件各45美元的图形T恤和一件30美元的包。
两支车队抵达拉斯维加斯时的位置截然不同。梅赛德斯在巴西大奖赛上锁定了2026年 constructors' championship。奥迪在接管萨博后作为一支工厂车队的第一赛季，目前排名第八，积28分。这家德国车队落后哈斯三分。
梅赛德斯车队的基米·安东内利在墨西哥大奖赛中赢得了车手冠军，成为F1历史上最年轻的冠军。他的队友乔治·拉塞尔目前正在争夺亚军，目前排名第三，落后红牛的马克斯·维斯塔潘。
奥迪的加布里埃尔·博尔特洛托和尼科·胡肯伯格目前在车手积分榜上分别排名第14和第15，两人都积14分。
拉斯维加斯大奖赛将于11月19日至21日举行，是赛季最后三轮比赛中的第一轮，紧接着是卡塔尔和阿布扎比。
detailEn: Mercedes and Audi unveil adidas collections for F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix
The Mercedes Neon Lights and Audi After Hours collections are available now through adidas.com
A rainbow above the Welcome to Las Vegas sign
Motorsport culture beyond the track. Driver lifestyle, fashion, travel, design and the stories that make racing more than a sport.
Mercedes and Audi have unveiled special adidas fan collections for the upcoming Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Mercedes' range is called "Neon Lights", while Audi's is named "After Hours". Both collections are available now through adidas.com, and the pieces listed on the brand's US store range in price from $30 to $200.
The most expensive items are the outerwear. Mercedes' Las Vegas jacket and Audi's Las Vegas bomber jacket both cost $200.
The Mercedes collection is the bigger of the two. Alongside the jacket, it includes a $120 hoodie, a $95 long-sleeve T-shirt, $60 shorts, a $55 driver cap, a $50 race cap and T-shirts at $40 and $45.
Audi's line-up has a $55 driver cap, two graphic T-shirts at $45 each and a $30 bag.

The two teams arrive in Las Vegas in very different positions. Mercedes secured the 2026 constructors' championship at the Brazilian Grand Prix. Audi, in its first season as a works team after taking over Sauber, currently sits eighth in the standings with 28 points. The German outfit is three points behind Haas.

Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli claimed the drivers' title at the Mexican Grand Prix, becoming the youngest champion in the history of F1. His team-mate George Russell is currently in the fight for second in the championship, sitting third behind Red Bull's Max Verstappen.
Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto and Nico Hulkenberg currently sit 14th and 15th in the drivers' standings, both on 14 points.
The Las Vegas Grand Prix takes place from 19 to 21 November and is the first of the final three rounds of the season, ahead of Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

relatedItems.summaryEn: Four-time Formula 1 world champion Max Verstappen has become the new ambassador of the VDK Group, a Dutch group of installation and technical companies, and will feature in its communications and marketing campaigns over the coming years.
detailZh: 马克斯·维斯塔潘与荷兰技术集团VDK签任大使协议
这位红牛车手将在未来数年参与VDK的传播与营销活动
致红牛车迷。关注红牛车队，获取来自米尔顿凯恩斯的F1新闻、车手动态、技术洞察与比赛分析。
四届F1世界冠军马克斯·维斯塔潘成为荷兰安装与技术企业集团VDK Group的新任大使，该集团正在向欧洲扩张。
这位荷兰车手将在未来几年在该公司的国际品牌推广中发挥重要作用，并将出现在其传播和营销活动中。
VDK 成立于 2013 年，是一家荷兰技术公司集团，如今在荷兰、德国、瑞典、奥地利、瑞士和比利时都有业务。
维斯塔潘表示，他认为 VDK 的组织方式与 F1 车队的运作方式有相似之处。
“VDK 的世界与一级方程式赛车之间有很多相似之处，”这位红牛车手说道。“技术发挥着巨大作用，但任何关注这项运动的人都知道，只有整个团队都达到顶尖水平，你才能发挥出最佳表现。”
在一支一级方程式车队里，每天都有大量的人在工作，让一切变得更好、更快。每个人都有自己的专业领域和职责。我在VDK的运作方式中看到了这一点。
它由许多技术公司和专业人士组成，他们各有专长，但团结在一起就更强大。VDK是一家创新型公司，也有着远大的国际雄心。我很高兴能在未来几年成为其中一员。
VDK创始人兼首席执行官弗兰斯·范德科尔克表示，这位荷兰人是公司下一步发展的理想人选。
“马克斯·维斯塔潘加入VDK集团让我无比自豪，”范德科尔克说。“马克斯多年来一直是世界上最顶尖的车手之一。但同样吸引我的是这背后的一切。仅靠天赋永远不够。你需要身边有优秀的人、相互信任、技术专长，以及每天变得更好的动力。这正是我在VDK集团所看到的。”
“我们通过整合实力雄厚的本地家族企业，并给予创业者自由发展的空间来实现增长。这一基础不会改变。与此同时，我们正日益将目光投向国门之外。”
“随着在荷兰、德国、瑞典、奥地利、瑞士和比利时拥有公司，我们正在形成一个日益国际化的集团。马克斯·维斯塔潘闻名世界，同时也体现了那种令人熟悉的荷兰务实态度和赢家心态。说实话，我无法想象还有谁比他更能代表我们希望带领VDK前进的方向。”
过去两年一直与VDK合作的前F1车手罗伯特·杜恩博斯将继续担任大使和演讲嘉宾。根据公告，他在协调与维斯塔潘的合作关系中发挥了关键作用。
“我非常高兴能与弗兰斯和VDK集团合作，”杜恩博斯解释道。“我们已经共同取得了伟大的成就，我也真正了解了VDK背后的人。如今我还能为这一下一步贡献力量，这让一切更加特别。”
“有了马克斯，VDK 集团当然就引进了一位真正独一档的人物。我很高兴我们现在为 VDK 集团携手合作，也非常期待未来的岁月。”
detailEn: Max Verstappen signs ambassador deal with Dutch technical group VDK
The Red Bull driver will feature in VDK’s communications and marketing campaigns over the coming years
For Red Bull fans. Keeping watch on Red Bull Racing, with F1 news, driver updates, technical insight and race analysis from Milton Keynes.
Four-time Formula 1 champion Max Verstappen has become the new ambassador of the VDK Group, a Dutch group of installation and technical companies that is expanding across Europe.
The Dutchman will play a prominent role in the company's international branding over the coming years and will feature in its communications and marketing campaigns.
VDK was founded in 2013 as a Dutch group of technical companies and now has businesses in the Netherlands, Germany, Sweden, Austria, Switzerland and Belgium.
Verstappen said he saw parallels between the way VDK is organised and the way an F1 team works.

"There are many similarities between the world of VDK and Formula 1," the Red Bull driver said. "Technology plays a huge role, but anyone who follows the sport knows that you can only perform at your best if the entire team is top-notch.

"In a Formula 1 team, a huge number of people work every day to make everything better and faster. Everyone has their own area of specialisation and responsibility. I recognise that in the way VDK operates.

"It’s a group of many technical companies and professionals who all have their own expertise but are stronger together. VDK is an innovative company and also has major international ambitions. I’m excited to be a part of that in the coming years."
VDK founder and chief executive Frans van der Kolk said the Dutchman was the ideal fit for the company's next step.

"The fact that Max Verstappen is joining the VDK Group makes me incredibly proud," van der Kolk said. "Max has been among the absolute world’s best for years. But what appeals to me just as much is what lies behind that. Talent alone is never enough. You need good people around you, mutual trust, technical expertise, and the drive to get better every day. That’s exactly what I see in the VDK Group.

"We’ve grown by bringing together strong local and family-owned businesses and giving entrepreneurs the freedom to thrive. That foundation won’t change. At the same time, we’re looking beyond our borders with increasing focus.

"With companies in the Netherlands, Germany, Sweden, Austria, Switzerland, and Belgium, we’re forming an increasingly international group. Max Verstappen is known worldwide and, at the same time, embodies that recognisable Dutch down-to-earth attitude and winner’s mentality. To be honest, I can’t imagine a stronger face to represent where we want to take VDK."

Former F1 driver Robert Doornbos, who has worked with VDK for the past two years, will stay on as an ambassador and speaker. According to the announcement, he played a key role in coordinating the partnership with Verstappen.

"I am very pleased with the collaboration with Frans and the VDK Group," Doornbos explained. "We’ve already achieved great things together, and I’ve really gotten to know the people behind VDK. The fact that I’ve now also been able to contribute to this next step makes it even more special.

"With Max, the VDK Group is, of course, bringing in someone who is truly in a league of his own. I’m happy that we’re now working together for the VDK Group and am really looking forward to the years ahead."
